title: Social Media Agency in Charleston, SC
metaTitle: Social Media Agency in Charleston, SC | TDM
metaDescription: Social media management for Charleston businesses: content, daily posting, replies and paid social for restaurants, inns, wedding vendors, shops and practices.
lead: TDM (The Digital Marketing Services) runs social media for Charleston businesses: strategy, content, posting, replies to comments and messages, and paid social. Charleston is photographed constantly, which is both the opportunity and the difficulty. Every visitor already posts Rainbow Row, the Pineapple Fountain and the Ravenel Bridge at sunset. A business has to show what only it can show, and we plan content around that.

sections.heading: Who follows a Charleston business
paragraphs: Visitors follow in the weeks before a trip and save posts as a to-do list. Content for them answers planning questions: what to reserve ahead, what the courtyard looks like, how long the tour lasts, how to get from the hotel to Shem Creek or Folly Beach.

Residents keep the doors open in January and August, and they care about other things. The weekday special, the new location in West Ashley, where to park, whether the kitchen is serving when the street outside has flooded at high tide. Neighbourhood Facebook groups in Mount Pleasant, Daniel Island, James Island and Summerville are where the name of a plumber or an orthodontist gets passed along.

Wedding couples use Instagram and Pinterest as a catalogue. They open a venue's tagged photos to find the florist, planner and photographer who have worked there, so tagging and crediting fellow vendors is part of the job and not a courtesy.
Employers are the fourth audience. The hospital systems, the plants in North Charleston and the firms around the port use LinkedIn and Facebook to show people they hope to hire what the work is like.

sections.heading: Content that could only come from here
paragraphs: We build a monthly calendar from your real diary: the start of oyster season, a new menu, a different tour route, a spring open house, a trunk show, Second Sunday on King Street, the festival weeks when the city fills.

Much of the raw material can be filmed by your own staff on a phone. We send a short shot list, then our editors cut the footage into Reels, Stories and TikToks, add captions and graphics, and schedule them. The real kitchen, boat or garden stays on screen without a film crew in town each week.
The plan also covers bad days. When a storm watch is issued or the streets downtown are under water, people check your page before they call. We agree in advance who posts what and how quickly.

sections.heading: The parts we can take over
paragraphs: Hand us every channel, or only editing, replies or advertising.
bullets: A plan for each platform: audience, tone, posting rhythm and what success means.
Graphics, captions, photo edits and short video for Instagram, Facebook, TikTok and LinkedIn.
Daily posting and profile upkeep, with content approved by you first.
Replies to comments, direct messages and reviews, with booking questions passed to your team.
Paid social on Meta, TikTok and LinkedIn to carry your strongest posts further.
A monthly report on reach, engagement, clicks and enquiries, with changes for the next month.

sections.heading: Questions worth asking first
paragraphs: Make sure the accounts and logins stay yours. Ask how fast a message is answered on a Saturday in April, when half the city is booked. Ask how the agency will get footage of a place it is not standing in. And ask about permission: wedding guests, patients and anything filmed inside a plant or terminal need consent or clearance before they appear in a post.

cards.heading: Where social media earns its keep in Charleston

items.title: Restaurants and bars
items.text: Dishes, specials and the room itself, shown often enough that visitors book ahead and locals come back midweek.

items.title: Inns, tours and charters
items.text: Short video of the actual experience, plus fast answers to the questions people send before they reserve.

items.title: Wedding vendors
items.text: Recent weddings posted with venues and fellow vendors tagged, so couples find you through the places they are considering.

items.title: Employers hiring
items.text: Posts about the work, the team and open roles for manufacturers, logistics firms and healthcare organisations.

presence: A member of our team is based in South Carolina rather than in Charleston, and planning, editing, posting and community management are done remotely by the wider TDM team, working from footage and photos your staff supply.

faqs.q: Can an agency that is not in Charleston manage our social media?
faqs.a: Yes, if the content still comes from your premises. A member of our team is based in South Carolina, and the rest of the work is remote. Your staff film short clips to our shot list, and we handle editing, captions, scheduling and replies.

faqs.q: Which platforms matter most for a Charleston wedding business?
faqs.a: Instagram and Pinterest are where couples collect ideas and discover vendors. Facebook still carries reviews and referrals from past clients and their families. TikTok suits behind-the-scenes video.

faqs.q: How much does social media management cost in Charleston?
faqs.a: It depends on the number of platforms, how many posts and videos you want each month and whether we also answer messages and run ads, so the quote follows a free consultation.

faqs.q: How long before social media brings bookings?
faqs.a: It depends on your requirements, the brief and where the accounts stand today, and the plan states what will be measured and over what period.
